This year I plan same as last year — no reason to change when it worked. My man is away doing construction work most months, so I handle the fields with my daughter-in-law helping in busy times.

I have 16.9 mu. Cotton is my main crop because the price has been okay and I know cotton — 35 years I grow it. I put cotton on 10 mu, the flat good land near the well. The other piece, about 5 mu, I do wheat in winter and maize after in summer — same land two crops, like everyone here does. The little corner, about 1.9 mu, is sandy and not so good, so I throw mungbean there — mungbean does not need much, and I can sell or keep for the house.

For fertilizer I buy what the shop has, the compound kind, 15-15-15 or similar. For cotton I use 2 bags per mu before planting, then one bag urea when flowers come — my neighbor Liu's wife does this and she gets good bolls. For wheat I do 2 bags compound before sowing, and topdressing urea in spring when it turns green. Maize same as wheat, maybe a bit more urea because maize eats a lot. Mungbean I hardly put anything — mungbean makes its own strength in the roots, my mother-in-law told me long ago.

Cotton needs much spray — bollworm, aphid, red spider. I spray many times, I lose count, maybe 7-8 times through the summer. Wheat just one or two times for aphid. Maize one time usually enough. Mungbean one spray if bugs come.

I water cotton from the well — 3 or 4 times in the hot months. Wheat needs water too, 2 or 3 times in spring. Maize 2 times. Mungbean one time if no rain.

Seeds — I buy from the same dealer in the town. Cotton is the improved kind, everyone around buys it. Maize must be hybrid, the packet kind, otherwise yield is poor. Wheat I use improved variety, save some seed from last year too. Mungbean I keep my own seed.

I rotary-till everything with the tractor rental man — 30 yuan per mu, cheaper than plowing deep.
